q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most: 34.6% of their videos outperformed their baseline (18 of 52 with a baseline, out of 70 videos), versus 23.1% for mid (9 of 39) and 5.3% for large (1 of 19, a very small base). Small channels' average lift is also highest at 5.4x, though a few big hits likely pull that up.

Audiences are broadly positive, but they differ by size:
- Mid: net sentiment +33 (52.7% positive, 20.0% negative), n=455 product-side comments
- Small: +26 (48.3% positive, 22.4% negative), n=693
- Large: +10 (42.8% positive, 33.0% negative), n=285

Large channels have the weakest breakout rate and the least happy audiences. Caveat: these are comment samples, and the large group has few videos (25), so treat its rate cautiously.
sql: WITH v AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), lift AS (SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(CASE WHEN outperformer IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS mean_rel_lift FROM v GROUP BY size_group), sent AS (SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') GROUP BY v.size_group) SELECT l.size_group, l.n_videos, l.n_with_baseline, l.outperformer_rate, l.mean_rel_lift, s.n_product_side, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative, s.net_sentiment FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_group=l.size_group ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions work best for mid-sized channels. They have the highest outperformer rate (44%, n=18) and the highest mean relative lift (2.37). Engagement is modest at 1.4%.

Explainer/tips come next, with a 17% outperformer rate (n=6), 1.13 lift, and the highest engagement of the larger groups at 2.4%.

Comparison videos had no outperformers (n=3), although their mean lift of 1.70 is fairly high. Upgrade advice (n=6), keynote recaps (n=2), other (n=3), and the single meme short had no outperformers and lifts below 1.

Caveat: every format except first impressions has very small n, so those rankings are tentative. These are associations, not causes.
sql: SELECT c.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(CASE WHEN p.rel_lift IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer), 3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift), 3) AS mean_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(p.eng_rate), 3) AS mean_eng_rate FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id = c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id = c.video_id WHERE c.topic = 'duo' AND c.format != 'official' AND cr.tier = 'mid 250k-1M' GROUP BY c.format HAVING n_with_baseline > 0 ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, mean_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
Two high-lift videos, both from Shawn Shaman, have the weakest audience reaction, and neither is strongly negative.

1. "Apple Tricked You With iPhone Duo" (meme short): net sentiment -7 (43% positive, 50% negative, n=14). Lift is 118.45 (rel_lift 9.5) on 181,226 views.

2. "Don't Buy The #iPhoneDuo... Here's Why" (upgrade advice): net sentiment 0 (31% positive, 31% negative, n=16). Lift is 135.85 (rel_lift 10.9) on 207,847 views.

Caveat: each video has only 14-16 product-side comments, so these scores are rough and could shift with a few comments. They show association, not that sentiment drives or hurts lift.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(c.sentiment='positive') AS pos, AVG(c.sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments c WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY c.video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT ct.video_id, ct.title, ct.url, cr.name AS creator, ct.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, p.outperformer, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pos-s.neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content ct JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=ct.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=ct.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=ct.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 2

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Largest topics overall: Praise for the video (n=209, 9.3% of comments), Samsung Fold comparisons (n=143, 6.4%), and High price (n=131, 5.8%).

Fastest growing this week (prior week n≥10 required):
- Samsung Fold comparisons: +367% (15 to 70)
- Cases and design: +241% (17 to 58)
- High price: +235% (17 to 57)
- Apple's approach and Android: +200% (15 to 45)
- Reasons not to buy: +190% (10 to 29)

Praise for the video is biggest but grew only 148% (29 to 72), ranking 6th in growth.

Several topics, such as Buy or don't buy (6 to 33) and Pre-order plans (9 to 33), also jumped but lack enough prior-week comments (n<10) to rank for growth. Treat those as directional only.

Caveat: this is a sample of English comments, and the counts show association, not cause.
sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cm.comment_id, cm.topic_id, cm.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM c), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_all FROM c), agg AS (SELECT c.topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN c.d > mx.m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, SUM(CASE WHEN c.d <= mx.m-7 AND c.d > mx.m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week FROM c, mx WHERE c.topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.topic_id), r AS (SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(a.n_total*1.0/tot.n_all,3) AS share_of_all_comments, a.n_this_week, a.n_prev_week, CASE WHEN a.n_prev_week>=10 THEN ROUND((a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week)*1.0/a.n_prev_week,3) END AS wow_growth FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot) SELECT r.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY n_total DESC) AS size_rank, CASE WHEN wow_growth IS NOT NULL THEN RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY (wow_growth IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY wow_growth DESC) END AS growth_rank FROM r ORDER BY n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
a:
Duo has by far the best sentiment: net +25 across 1,433 product-side comments on 127 videos (49% positive, 24% negative). Every other group scores lower.

- Competitor foldables: net 0 (36% positive, 36% negative), but only n=28 comments from 2 videos.
- Other products: net -10 (31% positive, 41% negative), n=51 from 6 videos.
- General event videos: net -15 (26% positive, 41% negative), n=76 from 8 videos.
- iPhone 18 Pro: only n=4 comments, so no score is reliable.

Duo's result rests on a large sample. The comparison groups are small, so treat their scores as rough directional signals. This is also a sample of comments, not all viewers.
sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(m.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(m.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) END AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY net_sentiment DESC LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Commenters like the fold animation most: net sentiment +73 (n=52), with 87% positive and 13% negative. Excitement about buying also stands out, with pre-order plans at +57 (n=44) and eagerness to buy at +41 (n=88).

Price draws the most criticism. It is the largest topic (n=117) and has the highest negative share at 36%, but opinion is split, with net sentiment at +3 (39% positive). The Duo vs iPhone 18 Pro Max debate (n=94) is similarly split at +2, with 31% negative.

Left-handed concerns are the only net-negative topic at -6, but n=34 is small.

Caveat: these are topic-level shares from a sample of comments, and many comments mix jokes with opinions.
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT c.topic_id, c.sentiment
  FROM comments c
  JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id
  WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official'
    AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0
    AND c.target IN ('product','price_value')
    AND c.topic_id IS NOT NULL
),
agg AS (
  SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary,
    COUNT(*) AS n_product_side,
    SUM(b.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos,
    SUM(b.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg,
    ROUND(1.0*SUM(b.sentiment='positive')/COUNT(*),3) AS pos_share,
    ROUND(1.0*SUM(b.sentiment='negative')/COUNT(*),3) AS neg_share
  FROM base b JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=b.topic_id
  WHERE t.pool='product'
  GROUP BY t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary
),
liked AS (
  SELECT 'most_liked' AS side, * FROM agg ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8
),
crit AS (
  SELECT 'most_criticised' AS side, * FROM agg ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8
)
SELECT * FROM liked
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM crit
